{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared for:** Customer (internal)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement  
**Findings reviewed:** 19 rules (all verified)

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. Eleven rules are compliant and require no redline, including the limitation of liability package (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence grant (§ 13), renewal mechanics (§ 8.2–8.3), Vendor warranties (§ 19), audit rights against us (§ 22), insurance (§ 18), and the absence of any exclusivity or Customer-payable liquidated damages.

Eight items require action. Two are critical and structural: the Agreement contains **no indemnity provision at all** — Section 20 is absent and Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 cross-refer to indemnification obligations that do not exist — and **§ 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable we pay to create**, leaving us only a revocable licence limited to the Order Form term. A cluster of Customer-side restraints is also unacceptable: a three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly without reduction or termination rights (§ 2.1), a 24-month post-term non-compete and a 24-month Customer-only no-hire (§ 12.4), and an open-ended disclose-and-match MFN (§ 7.2). Each of these contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. We also have no convenience termination right, no transition assistance or data-export mechanic, and a Singapore governing law clause in § 28.1 that conflicts with the New York exclusive jurisdiction already agreed in § 28.2.

The good news is that most cures are short and self-contained. Because § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as uncapped Excluded Claims, we have targeted the preferred indemnity rather than a fallback super-cap, which would reduce our existing protection.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 19.5 (Section 20 absent; cross-refs at §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5) | No Vendor IP indemnity anywhere; walk-away. Insert preferred Vendor defence/indemnity with notice, control and cooperation. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor owns all Deliverables; our licence is revocable, non-transferable and term-limited. Fails the fallback perpetual/irrevocable/sublicensable licence. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with 21.2–21.4) | Mutual cap at greater of 12-month Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; carve-outs uncapped. Payment carve-out reaches only undisputed Fees — noted, not redlined. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (second) | 24-month post-term non-compete, any product, any territory; walk-away and contradicts § 12.3. |
| High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | Customer-only, all Vendor employees, 24 months, no general-advertising carve-out; walk-away and contradicts § 12.3. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 2.1 (with Section 9, § 10.2) | No Customer convenience right in a multi-year term; § 2.1 denies termination rights. Walk-away. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Customer may assign to Affiliate or successor on notice; Vendor gated and no change-of-control repricing. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; § 7.2 handled under MFN, § 2.1 under MINCOMMIT. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 7.1 | No penalties, early-termination fees or Fee acceleration; § 22.2 is cost reimbursement and true-up only. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with 13.2–13.3, 24.1) | Affiliates and contractors covered; perpetual paid-up licence; revocation limited to uncured material breach. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 (conflicts with § 28.2) | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction; outside the accepted list and internally inconsistent. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Open-ended disclose-and-match before engaging another provider; no product, time or like-for-like limits. Walk-away. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay without reduction or termination rights. Walk-away. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 (§ 16.5 defers to a non-existent Section 11) | No transition period created and no Customer Data return or export duty. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with 22.2–22.3) | Once in 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor, no direct system access. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with 8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with 19.2–19.5) | Professional/workmanlike and conformance warranties with full remedy ladder. Non-hosted Deliverables carry 90 days rather than 12 months — noted, not redlined. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with 18.2) | CGL, workers' compensation, E&O USD 2m and cyber/privacy USD 5m, unconditional; certificates on request. |

## Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and cannot be accepted as drafted:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (Section 20 absent)** — we insert a preferred-level Vendor defence and indemnity covering IP infringement by the Services or Deliverables, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice, control and cooperation and a narrow limit on any Customer indemnity. We deliberately do not import the fallback 3x super-cap, because § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as uncapped Excluded Claims.
2. **§ 2.1 take-or-pay minimum** — three years at USD 2,000,000 per year with no reduction or termination rights. Replace with payment for usage and ordered Services only.
3. **§ 2.1 / Section 9 — no convenience exit** — add a numbered § 9.4 giving us a 30-day convenience termination with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, confirm Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term, and conform § 2.1 while keeping the no-reduction restriction intact.
4. **§ 12.4 non-compete** — strike the 24-month post-term, all-product, all-territory restraint; retained § 12.3 already preserves our freedom to operate.
5. **§ 12.4 non-solicit / no-hire** — replace the Customer-only covenant with a confirmation that we are under no such restriction. A mutual, 12-month, involvement-limited non-solicit with general-advertising carve-outs remains available as a fallback.
6. **§ 7.2 MFN** — replace the disclose-and-match obligation with an express statement that we owe no disclosure or matching duty.
7. **§ 28.1 governing law and venue** — replace Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction with New York law, leaving § 28.2's New York County exclusive jurisdiction intact.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline covering the seven walk-away items above, plus the two remaining action items: flipping Deliverable ownership to Customer in § 14.2 with an express assignment (Vendor keeps Vendor Technology under § 14.3 and the § 13.2 perpetual embedded-IP licence), and inserting a fallback-level exit clause in Section 10 (90 days' transition assistance and Customer Data export within 30 days of expiry or termination).
2. Flag to Vendor the drafting defects we identified so they can be corrected on the same turn: the absent Section 20 with live cross-references at §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5; § 16.5's deferral of Customer Data to a non-existent Section 11; Section 23 having no operative text; the duplicated § 12.4 numbering; and the § 28.1 / § 28.2 forum conflict.
3. Confirm with the business the expected spend profile, so we can assess whether any negotiated volume commitment is worth trading for pricing — noting the playbook fallback is a commitment no longer than the current 12-month term, with a 30-day reduction right and a true-up rather than take-or-pay.
4. On acceptance of the indemnity insert, verify that § 21.3's Excluded Claims treatment continues to leave the new indemnity uncapped, so our position is not narrowed by a later sub-cap.
5. We do not propose redlines on the eleven compliant rules. Two minor sub-elements are noted for awareness only: the § 21.3 payment carve-out reaches undisputed Fees rather than all amounts due, and non-hosted Deliverables carry a 90-day rather than 12-month conformance warranty."}
